## Purpose and status

This file runs the Part A analysis in the SAP (v0.2 draft): the trend in fixed three-class KCMO from 2014 to 2023, the KCMO definitions, and the data-quality checks that must pass before any trend is read. It returns aggregate tables only. No row-level data are written, displayed, or returned.

Status: draft. Analysis is not locked. Decisions D10 (highest-in-year as sensitivity) and D11 (EF below 40 percent) are applied as written in the SAP. Open questions for the registry team are listed in the README.

```{r setup}
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")
if (!file.exists(params$data_path)) stop("Set params$data_path (in the YAML or with quarto render -P data_path:<file>) to your extract.")
req <- c("dplyr", "tidyr", "ggplot2", "geepack", "knitr", "MetBrewer")
missing_pkgs <- req[!vapply(req, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing_pkgs) > 0) {
  stop("Install these packages first: install.packages(c(",
       paste(sprintf('"%s"', missing_pkgs), collapse = ", "), "))")
}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)

})
```

## Helper functions

Small-cell suppression: any row with a count between 1 and 9 has its statistics blanked before it is shown or written.

```{r helpers}
suppress_small <- function(df, count_cols) {
  # 1. any count of 1 to 9 is blanked (the count itself is disclosive)
  # 2. statistics in any row with a small count are blanked
  small <- rep(FALSE, nrow(df))
  for (v in count_cols) {
    cell <- !is.na(df[[v]]) & df[[v]] > 0 & df[[v]] < 10
    df[[v]][cell] <- NA
    small <- small | cell
  }
  stat_cols <- setdiff(names(df)[vapply(df, is.numeric, logical(1))], c(count_cols, "year", "threshold"))
  for (v in stat_cols) df[[v]][small] <- NA
  df
}

write_out <- function(df, name, count_cols = character(0)) {
  df <- suppress_small(df, count_cols)
  write.csv(df, file.path(params$outputs_dir, name), row.names = FALSE)
  invisible(df)
}

show_tab <- function(df, caption) {
  knitr::kable(df, caption = caption, digits = 2)
}

save_fig <- function(p, name, w = 7, h = 4.5) {
  print(p)
  ggsave(file.path(params$outputs_dir, "figures", paste0(name, ".png")), p,
         width = w, height = h, dpi = 150, bg = "white")
}
```

## 1. Target doses and substance mapping

Shared definitions live in `R/00_targets.R` (also used by the with-eligibility codebase). Primary targets are the shfdb4 target doses. ESC lowest-of-range is the secondary calculation: each drug has a `use_esc` flag, and `esc_all: true` switches every drug to ESC.

Status flags: `evidence` counts toward the score. `non_evidence` scores 0 for its class. `excluded` is excluded by decision (nebivolol): neither scored nor scored as 0. All metoprolol is treated as succinate (limitation). An ARNi dose of `0/0` is treated as not on ARNi (to be confirmed with Lina and Lars). Such a patient is still scored on the RAS slot if an ACEi or ARB is recorded as Yes. Kinapril is dropped for now. Dapagliflozin and empagliflozin have no shfdb4 target, so the SGLT2i class is binary.

```{r targets}
# Target table, class status, ARNi status, KCMO score, conflict and RAS rules
# (inlined from R/00_targets.R and R/02_score.R so this file runs on its own)
# 00_targets.R
# Target-dose table, substance mapping, and ARNi lookup for KCMO Part A.
# Shared by the with-eligibility and no-eligibility codebases.
#
# Conventions (decisions 2026-10-23):
#   * PRIMARY targets come from shfdb4 (not shfdb5; Lina's email).
#   * ESC lowest-of-range targets are kept as the SECONDARY calculation
#     (use_esc = TRUE per drug, or all drugs via esc_all).
#   * Nebivolol is EXCLUDED (status "excluded": not scored, not scored as 0).
#   * ALL metoprolol is treated as succinate (limitation: tartrate not separable).
#   * ARNi dose "0/0" is treated as NOT ON ARNi (pending review by Lina and Lars).
#     The RAS class still credits an ACEi or ARB recorded as Yes for that patient.
#   * Swedish spellings (Eplerenon, Spironalakton) are the registry strings
#     and map to the same targets as Eplerenone and Spironolactone.
#
# status_flag values:
#   "evidence"     counts toward the score
#   "non_evidence" scores 0 for its class
#   "excluded"     excluded by decision; neither scored nor scored as 0

tg <- function(cls, sub, flag, t4, te, uesc) {
  data.frame(class = cls, substance = sub, status_flag = flag,
             target_shfdb4 = as.numeric(t4), target_esc = as.numeric(te),
             use_esc = uesc, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

targets <- rbind(
  tg("ACEI", c("Captopril", "Enalapril", "Lisinopril", "Ramipril", "Trandolapril"), "evidence",
     c(150, 40, 35, 10, 4), c(150, 20, 20, 10, 4), c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE)),
  tg("ACEI", c("Cilazapril", "Fosinopril", "Perindopril"), "non_evidence",
     c(5, 40, 10), NA, FALSE),
  tg("ARB", c("Candesartan", "Losartan", "Valsartan"), "evidence",
     c(32, 150, 320), c(32, 150, 320), FALSE),
  tg("ARB", c("Eprosartan", "Irbesartan", "Telmisartan"), "non_evidence",
     c(600, 300, 80), NA, FALSE),
  # Beta-blockers: metoprolol treated as succinate; nebivolol excluded by decision.
  tg("BB", c("Bisoprolol", "Carvedilol", "Metoprolol"), "evidence",
     c(10, 100, 200), c(10, 50, 200), c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE)),
  tg("BB", "Nebivolol", "excluded", NA, NA, FALSE),
  tg("BB", c("Atenolol", "Betaxolol", "Labetalol", "Pindolol", "Propanolol", "Sotalol", "Timolol"),
     "non_evidence", c(100, 40, 400, 15, 640, 320, 60), NA, FALSE),
  tg("MRA", c("Eplerenone", "Spironolactone", "Eplerenon", "Spironalakton"), "evidence",
     c(50, 50, 50, 50), c(50, 50, 50, 50), c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE)),
  tg("SGLT2", c("Dapagliflozin", "Empagliflozin"), "evidence",
     c(NA, NA), c(10, 10), c(FALSE, FALSE)),   # no shfdb4 target: binary class (SAP 3.3)
  tg("SGLT2", c("Ertugliflozin", "Kanagliflozin"), "non_evidence",
     c(NA, NA), c(NA, NA), c(FALSE, FALSE))
)

# shfdb4 %TD for ARNi, keyed by the sacubitril/valsartan dose string (mg/24 h).
# "0/0" is handled separately by arni_status() (see zero_not_on).
arni_lookup <- data.frame(
  arnidose = c("24/26", "48/52", "49/51", "61/64", "73/77", "85/90", "97/103", "98/102",
               "121/129", "122/128", "145/155", "146/154", "157/168", "170/180",
               "194/206", "195/205", "218/232", "219/231", "242/258", "243/257",
               "267/283", "292/308", "316/334", "340/360"),
  pct_td = c(12, 25, 25, 31, 37, 44, 50, 50, 62, 62, 75, 75, 81, 87,
             100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

targets$evidence <- targets$status_flag == "evidence"

# Target table for one convention. esc_all = TRUE switches every drug to ESC.
mk_targets <- function(esc_all = FALSE) {
  t <- targets
  t$use_esc_eff <- if (esc_all) TRUE else t$use_esc
  t$target_eff <- ifelse(t$use_esc_eff, t$target_esc, t$target_shfdb4)
  t$target_eff[t$class == "SGLT2"] <- t$target_esc[t$class == "SGLT2"]
  t
}

# 02_score.R
# Class-level status, ARNi status, and KCMO assembly.
# Same logic for both codebases. Pass elig = NULL for the no-eligibility codebase
# (fixed denominator 3, or 4 from May 2021) or elig = elig_flags(...) for the
# with-eligibility codebase (denominator = eligible classes only).

class_status <- function(use, sub, dose, cls, captured, tt, weight) {
  tc <- tt[tt$class == cls, ]
  m <- match(sub, tc$substance)
  known <- !is.na(m)
  flag <- tc$status_flag[m]
  evid <- known & flag %in% "evidence"
  excl <- known & flag %in% "excluded"
  tgt  <- tc$target_eff[m]
  if (cls == "BB") {
    # ESC carvedilol weight rule (only when ESC is used for carvedilol); missing weight = 50
    cv <- known & sub %in% "Carvedilol" & (tc$use_esc_eff[m] %in% TRUE)
    cv[is.na(cv)] <- FALSE
    tgt[cv] <- ifelse(!is.na(weight[cv]) & weight[cv] > 85, 100, 50)
  }
  st <- rep("unknown", length(use))
  st[!captured] <- "not_captured"
  no  <- captured & !is.na(use) & use == "No"
  yes <- captured & !is.na(use) & use == "Yes"
  st[no] <- "not_on"
  st[yes & is.na(sub)] <- "unknown"
  st[yes & !is.na(sub) & !known] <- "unmapped"
  st[yes & excl] <- "excluded"
  st[yes & known & !evid & !excl] <- "non_evidence"
  st[yes & evid & is.na(dose)] <- "dose_missing"
  st[yes & evid & !is.na(dose) & is.na(tgt)] <- "no_target"
  st[yes & evid & !is.na(dose) & !is.na(tgt)] <- "on"

  valid <- st %in% c("on", "not_on", "non_evidence")
  p   <- rep(NA_real_, length(st))
  raw <- rep(NA_real_, length(st))
  on  <- st == "on"
  raw[on] <- dose[on] / tgt[on]
  p[on]   <- pmin(1, raw[on])
  if (cls == "SGLT2") p[on] <- 1                  # binary class (SAP 3.3)
  p[st %in% c("not_on", "non_evidence")] <- 0
  list(st = st, valid = valid, p = p, raw = raw)
}

# ARNi status. zero_not_on = TRUE: dose "0/0" is treated as NOT on ARNi
# (decision 2026-10-23, to be reviewed with Lina and Lars). Flagged in zero_00.
# The RAS slot (ACEi, ARB, or ARNi) takes the maximum of the three, so a 0/0 patient
# still gets credit for an ACEi or ARB recorded as Yes.
arni_status <- function(use, dose_str, captured, zero_not_on = TRUE) {
  st <- rep("unknown", length(use))
  st[!captured] <- "not_captured"
  no  <- captured & !is.na(use) & use == "No"
  yes <- captured & !is.na(use) & use == "Yes"
  zero_00 <- yes & !is.na(dose_str) & dose_str == "0/0"
  st[no] <- "not_on"
  st[yes & is.na(dose_str)] <- "dose_missing"
  st[zero_00] <- if (zero_not_on) "not_on" else "dose_missing"
  st[yes & !is.na(dose_str) & dose_str != "0/0" & !(dose_str %in% arni_lookup$arnidose)] <- "unmapped"
  st[yes & !is.na(dose_str) & dose_str %in% arni_lookup$arnidose] <- "on"
  pct <- arni_lookup$pct_td[match(dose_str, arni_lookup$arnidose)] / 100
  p   <- rep(NA_real_, length(st))
  p[st == "on"]     <- pmin(1, pct[st == "on"])
  p[st == "not_on"] <- 0
  raw <- rep(NA_real_, length(st))
  raw[st == "on"] <- pct[st == "on"]
  list(st = st, valid = st %in% c("on", "not_on"), p = p, raw = raw, zero_00 = zero_00)
}

# KCMO = 100 * sum(p over scored classes) / (number of scored classes).
# cs: list(ras, bb, mra, sg), each list(valid, p).
# use_sg: logical per row, TRUE once the SGLT2i class is in the score (from May 2021).
# elig: NULL, or list(ras, bb, mra, sg) of TRUE / FALSE / NA from elig_flags().
#   NULL  -> every class scored (fixed denominator).
#   FALSE -> class not scored for that row (removed from numerator and denominator).
#   NA    -> eligibility unknown: row not scored (counted in flow).
kcmo_score <- function(cs, use_sg, elig = NULL) {
  n <- length(cs$ras$p)
  inc <- list(ras = rep(TRUE, n), bb = rep(TRUE, n), mra = rep(TRUE, n), sg = use_sg)
  ok  <- rep(TRUE, n)
  num <- rep(0, n)
  den <- rep(0, n)
  for (k in c("ras", "bb", "mra", "sg")) {
    e <- if (is.null(elig)) rep(TRUE, n) else elig[[k]]
    if (!is.null(elig)) ok <- ok & !(inc[[k]] & is.na(e))           # unknown eligibility
    inscore <- inc[[k]] & (e %in% TRUE)
    ok  <- ok & !(inscore & !cs[[k]]$valid)                         # invalid status
    num <- num + ifelse(inscore & cs[[k]]$valid, cs[[k]]$p, 0)
    den <- den + inscore
  }
  ok <- ok & den > 0
  ifelse(ok, 100 * num / den, NA_real_)
}

# Rows removed for same-row RAS conflicts (shared by both codebases).
# ACEi with ARB is always a conflict. ARNi counts only at a non-zero dose:
# a 0/0 ARNi dose means not on ARNi, so it does not conflict with an ACEi or ARB.
conflict_rows <- function(d) {
  yes1 <- function(x) !is.na(x) & x == "Yes"
  arni_on <- yes1(d$shf_arni) & !(d$shf_arnidose %in% "0/0")
  (yes1(d$shf_acei) & yes1(d$shf_arb)) |
    (yes1(d$shf_arb) & arni_on) |
    (yes1(d$shf_acei) & arni_on)
}

# RAS slot: best of ACEi, ARB, or ARNi. Valid when ACEi and ARB are valid and
# the ARNi status is valid or not yet captured. A 0/0 ARNi is not_on (valid, p = 0),
# so the patient keeps credit from a recorded ACEi or ARB.
ras_slot <- function(acei, arb, arni) {
  valid <- acei$valid & arb$valid & (arni$st == "not_captured" | arni$valid)
  list(valid = valid,
       p = ifelse(valid, pmax(acei$p, arb$p, arni$p, na.rm = TRUE), NA_real_))
}

tt <- mk_targets(params$esc_all)
```

## 2. Row-level status for each class

Each row gets a status per class (functions `class_status()` and `arni_status()` in `R/02_score.R`). Only "on", "not_on", and "non_evidence" count as valid. Everything else (unknown, unmapped, dose missing, no target, excluded) is left out of the score and counted in the flow table, not silently scored as zero.

- `not_on`: use = No, and the field was captured. For ARNi, a `0/0` dose is also `not_on`, and the patient can still receive RAS credit from an ACEi or ARB.
- `non_evidence`: use = Yes with a non-evidence agent. Scored 0 for the class.
- `excluded`: use = Yes with an excluded agent (nebivolol). Not scored; the row is left out of the score for that class.
- `not_captured`: before the field's capture date. Treated as unknown, not as No.

## 3. Building the analysis rows

Filters in order, with counts kept for the flow table: calendar year 2014 to year_max; one row per patient per visit date; outpatient rows; EF below 40 percent; HF duration at least 90 days; no same-row combination of ACEi with ARB, and no same-row combination of ACEi or ARB with an ARNi at a non-zero dose (a `0/0` ARNi dose is not an ARNi, so it does not create a conflict). Then the class scores are computed and the three-class and four-class KCMO are assigned to rows that have complete, valid statuses.

KCMO = 100 × (sum of class scores) / (number of score classes). Every class is eligible in this version (SAP L1, eligibility deferred), so the denominator is 3 for the fixed series and 4 for the SGLT2i series.

```{r build-rows}
build_rows <- function(dat, esc_all) {
  tt <- mk_targets(esc_all)
  d <- dat
  d$date <- as.Date(d$shf_indexdtm)
  d$year <- as.integer(format(d$date, "%Y"))
  cnt <- function(x) as.integer(table(factor(x, levels = yrs)))

  d <- d[d$year %in% yrs, ]
  d <- d[!duplicated(paste(d$lopnr, d$date)), ]
  flow <- data.frame(year = yrs, rows_window_dedup = cnt(d$year))

  d <- d[!is.na(d$shf_location) & d$shf_location == params$outpatient_value, ]
  flow$rows_outpatient <- cnt(d$year)

  # LB comment: see previous code comment about continous and categorical EF
  d <- d[!is.na(d$shf_ef) & d$shf_ef %in% c("<30", "30-39") & !is.na(d$sos_durationhf) & d$sos_durationhf >= 90, ] 
  flow$rows_ef_duration <- cnt(d$year)

  yes1 <- function(x) !is.na(x) & x == "Yes"
  conflict <- conflict_rows(d)   # R/02_score.R: 0/0 ARNi does not conflict
  d <- d[!conflict, ]
  flow$rows_no_conflict <- cnt(d$year)

  n <- nrow(d)
  arni_cap <- d$date >= as.Date("2016-04-20")
  sg_cap   <- d$date >= as.Date("2021-04-28")
  acei <- class_status(d$shf_acei, d$shf_aceisub, d$shf_aceidose, "ACEI", rep(TRUE, n), tt, d$shf_weight)
  arb  <- class_status(d$shf_arb,  d$shf_arbsub,  d$shf_arbdose,  "ARB",  rep(TRUE, n), tt, d$shf_weight)
  bb   <- class_status(d$shf_bbl,  d$shf_bblsub,  d$shf_bbldose,  "BB",   rep(TRUE, n), tt, d$shf_weight)
  mra  <- class_status(d$shf_mra,  d$shf_mrasub,  d$shf_mradose,  "MRA",  rep(TRUE, n), tt, d$shf_weight)
  sg   <- class_status(d$shf_sglt2i, d$shf_sglt2isub, d$shf_sglt2idose, "SGLT2", sg_cap, tt, d$shf_weight)
  arni <- arni_status(d$shf_arni, d$shf_arnidose, arni_cap)

  # RAS slot: ACEi, ARB, or ARNi. ARNi is ignored before its capture date.
  rs     <- ras_slot(acei, arb, arni)   # R/02_score.R
  ras_ok <- rs$valid
  ras_p  <- rs$p
  ras_on <- ras_ok & (acei$st == "on" | arb$st == "on" | arni$st == "on")
  ras_raw <- pmax(acei$raw, arb$raw, arni$raw, na.rm = TRUE)

  k3_ok <- ras_ok & bb$valid & mra$valid
  kcmo3 <- ifelse(k3_ok, 100 * (ras_p + bb$p + mra$p) / 3, NA_real_)
  k4_ok <- k3_ok & sg$valid & (d$date >= as.Date("2021-05-01"))
  kcmo4 <- ifelse(k4_ok, 100 * (ras_p + bb$p + mra$p + sg$p) / 4, NA_real_)

  # Stop rule: share of population rows with any class raw %TD above 2 (before the 100% cap).
  raw_any <- pmax(ras_raw, bb$raw, mra$raw, sg$raw, na.rm = TRUE)
  over2 <- !is.na(raw_any) & raw_any > 2

  rows <- data.frame(
    lopnr = d$lopnr, date = d$date, year = d$year,
    age = d$shf_age, female = as.integer(d$shf_sex == "Female"),
    nyha_hi = ifelse(is.na(d$shf_nyha), NA, d$shf_nyha %in% c("III", "IV")),
    dig = d$shf_digoxin == "Yes", ivab = d$shf_sinusnodei == "Yes", nitr = d$shf_nitrate == "Yes",
    ras_ok = ras_ok, ras_on = ras_on, p_ras = ras_p,
    bb_valid = bb$valid, bb_on = bb$st == "on", p_bb = bb$p,
    mra_valid = mra$valid, mra_on = mra$st == "on", p_mra = mra$p,
    sg_valid = sg$valid & d$date >= as.Date("2021-05-01"), sg_on = sg$st == "on", p_sg = sg$p,
    k3_ok = k3_ok, kcmo3 = kcmo3, kcmo4 = kcmo4,
    over2 = over2,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  pop <- d  # population rows for completeness and mapping checks
  pop$st_acei <- acei$st; pop$st_arb <- arb$st; pop$st_arni <- arni$st
  pop$st_bb <- bb$st; pop$st_mra <- mra$st; pop$st_sg <- sg$st
  list(rows = rows, pop = pop, flow = flow, over2 = over2, n_pop = n)
}

P <- build_rows(
  if (grepl("\\.(RData|rda)$", params$data_path, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
    e <- new.env(); load(params$data_path, envir = e); get(ls(e)[1], envir = e)
  } else {
    read.csv(params$data_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  },
  params$esc_all
)
rows <- P$rows
pop  <- P$pop
cat("Population rows (outpatient, EF < 40, duration >= 90 days, no ACEi/ARB/ARNi conflict):", P$n_pop, "\n")
```

## 4. Data-quality checks (run before any trend is read)

### 4.1 Structure and flow

The flow table shows how many rows survive each filter in each year. Rows removed for missing or unmapped data are counted, not dropped silently.

```{r flow}
pick_py <- function(df, val_col, rule = c("latest", "highest", "first")) {
  rule <- match.arg(rule)
  x <- df[!is.na(df[[val_col]]), ]
  x$val <- x[[val_col]]
  x <- x[order(x$lopnr, x$year, x$date), ]
  if (rule == "latest")  x <- x %>% group_by(lopnr, year) %>% slice_tail(n = 1) %>% ungroup()
  if (rule == "first")   x <- x %>% group_by(lopnr, year) %>% slice_head(n = 1) %>% ungroup()
  if (rule == "highest") x <- x %>% group_by(lopnr, year) %>% slice_max(order_by = val, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup()
  x
}

py3 <- pick_py(rows, "kcmo3", "latest")
py3_high <- pick_py(rows, "kcmo3", "highest")
py3_first <- pick_py(rows, "kcmo3", "first")
py4 <- pick_py(rows, "kcmo4", "latest")

flow <- P$flow
flow$rows_kcmo3_valid <- as.integer(table(factor(rows$year[rows$k3_ok], levels = yrs)))
flow$patient_years_primary <- as.integer(table(factor(py3$year, levels = yrs)))
flow$patients_primary_all_years <- length(unique(py3$lopnr))
write_out(flow, "flow_by_year.csv", c("rows_window_dedup", "rows_outpatient", "rows_ef_duration",
                                      "rows_no_conflict", "rows_kcmo3_valid", "patient_years_primary"))
show_tab(suppress_small(flow, c("rows_window_dedup", "rows_outpatient", "rows_ef_duration",
                                 "rows_no_conflict", "rows_kcmo3_valid", "patient_years_primary")),
         "Rows and patient-years by calendar year (counts under 10 suppressed)")
```

### 4.2 Mapping: every substance in the population

Each substance found in the population is listed with its status: in the score (evidence-based), in the table as non-evidence, or not in the table. Anything not in the table must be resolved before the first run.

```{r mapping}
map_one <- function(use, sub, cls, tt) {
  x <- data.frame(use = use, sub = sub, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  x <- x[!is.na(x$use) & x$use == "Yes" & !is.na(x$sub), ]
  if (nrow(x) == 0) return(NULL)
  x %>% group_by(sub) %>% summarise(n_rows = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(class = cls)
}
mapping <- bind_rows(
  map_one(pop$shf_acei, pop$shf_aceisub, "ACEI", targets),
  map_one(pop$shf_arb, pop$shf_arbsub, "ARB", targets),
  map_one(pop$shf_bbl, pop$shf_bblsub, "BB", targets),
  map_one(pop$shf_mra, pop$shf_mrasub, "MRA", targets),
  map_one(pop$shf_sglt2i, pop$shf_sglt2isub, "SGLT2", targets)
) %>%
  left_join(targets %>% select(substance, evidence, status_flag, target_shfdb4, target_esc), by = c("sub" = "substance")) %>%
  mutate(status = case_when(
    is.na(evidence) ~ "NOT IN TABLE (resolve before run)",
    status_flag %in% "excluded" ~ "excluded by decision",
    evidence & is.na(target_shfdb4) & class != "SGLT2" ~ "in score, no shfdb4 target (Q11)",
    evidence ~ "in score",
    TRUE ~ "non-evidence (scores 0)")) %>%
  rename(substance = sub) %>%
  arrange(class, substance)
write_out(mapping, "mapping_check.csv", "n_rows")
show_tab(mapping, "Substances in the population and their mapping status")
```

### 4.3 ARNi parse check

The sacubitril component of the dose string should match the shfdb4 %TD lookup within 2 percentage points, with the shfdb4 cap at 100 percent applied (doses at or above 194 mg are all 100 percent in shfdb4). Mismatches would indicate a parse or lookup problem. Please confirm the cap with the registry team (Q6).

```{r arni-parse}
arni_chk <- pop[pop$st_arni == "on", ]
arni_chk$comp <- as.numeric(sub("/.*", "", arni_chk$shf_arnidose))
arni_chk$pct_parse <- pmin(100, 100 * arni_chk$comp / 194)  # shfdb4 caps all doses at or above 194 mg at 100 percent
arni_chk$year <- as.integer(format(arni_chk$shf_indexdtm, "%Y"))
arni_chk$pct_lookup <- arni_lookup$pct_td[match(arni_chk$shf_arnidose, arni_lookup$arnidose)]
arni_chk$mismatch <- abs(arni_chk$pct_parse - arni_chk$pct_lookup) > 2
arni_parse <- arni_chk %>% filter(!is.na(year)) %>% group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(n_on = n(), n_mismatch = sum(mismatch), .groups = "drop")
write_out(arni_parse, "arni_parse_check.csv", "n_on")
show_tab(suppress_small(arni_parse, "n_on"), "ARNi parse check by year (rows with 2 or more percentage points difference)")
```

### 4.4 shfdb4 versus ESC targets

Where the two conventions differ, the primary (shfdb4) and sensitivity (ESC) results will differ. Carvedilol under ESC depends on weight, so it is listed separately.

```{r target-diff}
diff_tab <- targets %>%
  filter(!is.na(target_shfdb4) & !is.na(target_esc) & target_shfdb4 != target_esc) %>%
  select(class, substance, target_shfdb4, target_esc, use_esc)
n_users <- pop %>% summarise(
  Enalapril = sum(shf_aceisub %in% "Enalapril", na.rm = TRUE),
  Lisinopril = sum(shf_aceisub %in% "Lisinopril", na.rm = TRUE),
  Carvedilol = sum(shf_bblsub %in% "Carvedilol", na.rm = TRUE))
diff_tab$n_rows_population <- c(n_users$Enalapril, n_users$Lisinopril, n_users$Carvedilol)[match(diff_tab$substance, c("Enalapril", "Lisinopril", "Carvedilol"))]
diff_tab$note <- ifelse(diff_tab$substance == "Carvedilol",
                        "ESC: 50 mg if weight 85 kg or less, 100 mg if above; missing weight uses 50",
                        "")
write_out(diff_tab, "shfdb4_vs_esc.csv", "n_rows_population")
show_tab(diff_tab, "Target differences between shfdb4 (primary) and ESC lowest-of-range (sensitivity)")
```

### 4.5 Stop rule

Share of population rows with any class dose above 2 times the target, before the 100 percent cap. If this exceeds 1 percent, the run stops and the mapping is reviewed before any trend is reported.

```{r stop-rule}
stop_tab <- data.frame(
  population_rows = P$n_pop,
  rows_any_class_over_2x = sum(P$over2),
  share_over_2x = round(mean(P$over2), 4),
  threshold = 0.01,
  halt = mean(P$over2) > 0.01
)
write_out(stop_tab, "stop_rule.csv")
show_tab(stop_tab, "Stop rule: dose-plausibility check")
if (params$halt_on_stop && stop_tab$halt) {
  stop("STOP RULE TRIGGERED: more than 1% of population rows have a dose above 2x target. ",
       "Review the mapping table and the dose fields with the registry team before running trends. ",
       "Send outputs/stop_rule.csv and outputs/mapping_check.csv back.")
}
```

## 5. Trend analysis (Part A)

### 5.1 KCMO by year

Fixed three-class KCMO uses the same classes in every year (comparability check). The era-standardized series uses the fixed three-class score through 2020 and the four-class score from May 2021 onward (SAP §5). 2021 is a partial year for the four-class series.

```{r kcmo-trend}
kby <- py3 %>% group_by(year) %>% summarise(
  n_py = n(),
  mean_fixed3 = mean(val), median_fixed3 = median(val),
  p10 = quantile(val, 0.1, names = FALSE), p25 = quantile(val, 0.25, names = FALSE),
  p75 = quantile(val, 0.75, names = FALSE), p90 = quantile(val, 0.9, names = FALSE),
  .groups = "drop")

kby4 <- py4 %>% group_by(year) %>% summarise(n_py_4class = n(), mean_4class = mean(val), .groups = "drop")

era_py <- bind_rows(
  py3 %>% filter(year < 2021) %>% mutate(era_val = val),
  py4 %>% filter(year >= 2021) %>% mutate(era_val = val)
)
kby_era <- era_py %>% group_by(year) %>% summarise(mean_era = mean(era_val), .groups = "drop")

# Direct age-sex standardization to the pooled 2014 to year_max mix (SAP §6.1)
py3$agegrp <- cut(py3$age, c(-Inf, 65, 75, Inf), labels = c("<65", "65-74", "75+"))
py3$strat <- paste(py3$agegrp, py3$female)
w <- prop.table(table(py3$strat))
sm <- py3 %>% group_by(year, strat) %>% summarise(m = mean(val), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
sm$m[sm$n < 10] <- NA
sm$w <- as.numeric(w[sm$strat])
std <- sm %>% group_by(year) %>% summarise(
  mean_std_agesex = if (n() == length(w) && all(!is.na(m))) sum(w * m) / sum(w) else NA_real_,
  .groups = "drop")

kcmo_tab <- kby %>% left_join(kby_era, by = "year") %>% left_join(kby4, by = "year") %>% left_join(std, by = "year")
kcmo_tab <- kcmo_tab %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric) & !matches("^n_"), ~ round(.x, 2)))
write_out(kcmo_tab, "kcmo_by_year.csv", c("n_py", "n_py_4class"))
show_tab(suppress_small(kcmo_tab, c("n_py", "n_py_4class")),
         "KCMO by calendar year (primary: latest qualifying row per patient-year)")
```

```{r fig-kcmo, fig.cap = "Fixed three-class KCMO by year: mean with interquartile range (primary, latest row per patient-year)."}
p1 <- kby %>% filter(n_py >= 10) %>%
  ggplot(aes(year, mean_fixed3)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p25, ymax = p75), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = yrs) +
  labs(x = "Calendar year", y = "KCMO Score") +
  theme_minimal()
save_fig(p1, "fig1_kcmo_fixed3")
```

### 5.3 Breadth versus depth (descriptive)

Breadth is the number of the three fixed classes on therapy (0 to 3). Depth is the mean percent of target across the classes on therapy. This is a descriptive table only; the outcome test belongs to Part B.

```{r breadth}
py3$n_on <- (py3$p_ras > 0) + (py3$p_bb > 0) + (py3$p_mra > 0)
breadth <- py3 %>% group_by(year, n_on) %>% summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(year) %>% mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>% ungroup()

  mutate(depth = (p_ras + p_bb + p_mra) / n_on) %>%
  group_by(year) %>% summarise(n_py_on = n(), mean_depth_pct = round(100 * mean(depth), 1), .groups = "drop")
```

### 5.4 Gap decomposition (descriptive)

Each class contributes (100/3) × (1 − score) to the gap from 100. The part from classes at 0 is underuse (including non-evidence agents, which score 0). The part from classes between 0 and 100 percent is underdosing. Totals reconcile to 100 − KCMO, shown as a check.

```{r gap}
u <- function(p) (100 / 3) * (p == 0)
dd <- function(p) (100 / 3) * (1 - p) * (p > 0 & p < 1)
py3$gap_underuse <- u(py3$p_ras) + u(py3$p_bb) + u(py3$p_mra)
py3$gap_underdose <- dd(py3$p_ras) + dd(py3$p_bb) + dd(py3$p_mra)
gap_tab <- py3 %>% group_by(year) %>% summarise(
  n_py = n(),
  mean_gap = round(mean(100 - val), 2),
  mean_underuse = round(mean(gap_underuse), 2),
  mean_underdosing = round(mean(gap_underdose), 2),
  reconciles = abs(mean(100 - val) - mean(gap_underuse + gap_underdose)) < 1e-6,
  .groups = "drop")
write_out(gap_tab, "gap_decomposition_by_year.csv", "n_py")
show_tab(suppress_small(gap_tab, "n_py"), "Gap from 100 decomposed into underuse and underdosing (mean points)")
```

```{r fig-gap, fig.cap = "Gap from 100 by year, split into underuse and underdosing."}
p4 <- gap_tab %>% filter(n_py >= 10) %>%
  select(year, mean_underuse, mean_underdosing) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(mean_underuse, mean_underdosing), names_to = "component", values_to = "points") %>%
  mutate(component = case_when(component == "mean_underuse" ~ "Underuse", TRUE ~ "Underdosing")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(year, points, fill = component)) +
  geom_area() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = yrs) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = okabe_ito[1:2]) +
  labs(x = "Calendar year", y = "Mean gap (points)", fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
save_fig(p4, "fig4_gap")
```

## 6. Titration and down-titration (descriptive, SAP §6.7)

RAS, beta-blocker, and MRA only. SGLT2i is binary in this analysis, so titration does not apply to it.

Patient-classes with at least two valid rows. Reached: peak score at or above 0.50 (or 1.00). Reduction: a later valid row with the class still in use and the score at least 0.25 below the peak. Discontinuation after reaching the threshold is counted separately. The registry has no reason-for-reduction field, so these are dose changes, not documented intolerance.

```{r titration}
rr <- rows[rows$ras_ok, ]
tl <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(lopnr = rr$lopnr, date = rr$date, cls = "RAS", p = rr$p_ras, on = rr$ras_on, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
  data.frame(lopnr = rows$lopnr[rows$bb_valid], date = rows$date[rows$bb_valid], cls = "BB",
             p = rows$p_bb[rows$bb_valid], on = rows$bb_on[rows$bb_valid], stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
  data.frame(lopnr = rows$lopnr[rows$mra_valid], date = rows$date[rows$mra_valid], cls = "MRA",
             p = rows$p_mra[rows$mra_valid], on = rows$mra_on[rows$mra_valid], stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
  NULL   # SGLT2i is binary (on = 1): titration does not apply
)
tl <- tl[order(tl$lopnr, tl$cls, tl$date), ]
tl$n_valid <- ave(seq_len(nrow(tl)), tl$lopnr, tl$cls, FUN = length)
tl$peak <- ave(tl$p, tl$lopnr, tl$cls, FUN = cummax)
tl2 <- tl[tl$n_valid >= 2, ]

tit_one <- function(thr) {
  key <- paste(tl2$lopnr, tl2$cls)
  res <- lapply(split(tl2, key), function(z) {
    hi <- z$peak >= thr
    red <- hi & z$on & z$p <= z$peak - 0.25
    t_reach <- if (any(hi)) min(z$date[hi]) else as.Date(NA)
    t_red <- if (any(red)) min(z$date[red]) else as.Date(NA)
    disc <- if (is.na(t_reach)) FALSE else any(hi & !z$on & z$date > t_reach)
    data.frame(cls = z$cls[1], reached = !is.na(t_reach), reduced = !is.na(t_red),
               days_to_reduction = if (!is.na(t_red) && !is.na(t_reach)) as.numeric(t_red - t_reach) else NA_real_,
               discontinued = disc, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  })
  pc <- do.call(rbind, res)
  pc %>% group_by(cls) %>% summarise(
    n_patient_classes = n(),
    n_reached = sum(reached),
    n_reduced = sum(reduced & reached),
    pct_reduced_of_reached = round(100 * sum(reduced & reached) / sum(reached), 1),
    median_days_to_reduction = round(median(days_to_reduction, na.rm = TRUE), 0),
    n_discontinued = sum(discontinued),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(threshold = thr)
}
tit <- bind_rows(tit_one(0.5), tit_one(1.0))
write_out(tit, "titration_summary.csv", c("n_patient_classes", "n_reached", "n_reduced", "n_discontinued"))
show_tab(suppress_small(tit, c("n_patient_classes", "n_reached", "n_reduced", "n_discontinued")),
         "Titration and down-titration (threshold 0.50 and 1.00 of target; counts under 10 suppressed)")
```

## 7. Within-patient change (descriptive, SAP §6.6)

Patients with at least two valid three-class rows: change from first to last valid value. Descriptive only.

```{r within}
vr <- rows[rows$k3_ok, ]
vr <- vr[order(vr$lopnr, vr$date), ]
pt <- vr %>% group_by(lopnr) %>% summarise(
  n_valid = n(), first_val = kcmo3[1], last_val = kcmo3[n()],
  d_first = min(date), d_last = max(date), .groups = "drop")
multi <- pt %>% filter(n_valid >= 2) %>% mutate(
  delta = last_val - first_val,
  years_between = as.numeric(d_last - d_first) / 365.25,
  change = case_when(abs(delta) < 5 ~ "stable",
                     abs(delta) <= 10 ~ "modest",
                     TRUE ~ "large"),
  direction = case_when(delta > 0 ~ "up", delta < 0 ~ "down", TRUE ~ "no change"))
within_sum <- data.frame(
  patients_any_valid = nrow(pt),
  patients_2plus_valid = nrow(multi),
  pct_2plus = round(100 * nrow(multi) / nrow(pt), 1),
  median_valid_rows_2plus = median(multi$n_valid),
  median_years_first_to_last = round(median(multi$years_between), 2),
  pct_change_stable_under5 = round(100 * mean(multi$change == "stable"), 1),
  pct_change_modest_5to10 = round(100 * mean(multi$change == "modest"), 1),
  pct_change_large_over10 = round(100 * mean(multi$change == "large"), 1),
  pct_up = round(100 * mean(multi$direction == "up"), 1),
  pct_down = round(100 * mean(multi$direction == "down"), 1),
  median_change_points = round(median(multi$delta), 2),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
rows_dist <- data.frame(
  valid_rows = c("1", "2", "3", "4 or more"),
  n_patients = as.integer(table(cut(pt$n_valid, c(0, 1, 2, 3, Inf), labels = c("1", "2", "3", "4 or more"))))
)
write_out(within_sum, "within_patient_change.csv", c("patients_any_valid", "patients_2plus_valid"))
write_out(rows_dist, "valid_rows_per_patient.csv", "n_patients")
show_tab(suppress_small(within_sum, c("patients_any_valid", "patients_2plus_valid")), "Within-patient change in fixed three-class KCMO")
show_tab(suppress_small(rows_dist, "n_patients"), "Valid rows per patient")
```

```{r fig-within, fig.cap = "Within-patient change in fixed three-class KCMO (last minus first valid row)."}
p5 <- multi %>% ggplot(aes(delta)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, boundary = 0) +
  labs(x = "Change in KCMO Score", y = "Patients") +
  theme_minimal()
save_fig(p5, "fig5_within_change")
```

## 8. Trend models (SAP §7.2)

Primary model: GEE on one row per patient-year, identity link, exchangeable correlation, clustered by patient. Calendar year is continuous. Adjusted for age, sex, and NYHA class (complete cases). Change is reported as the difference from 2014 to the last year in the data (span set by the data, currently 9 years). Piecewise slopes use known era boundaries (2016, 2021, 2024), not estimated joinpoints. The 2024 hinge is dropped and its era reported as not estimable when the extract has no 2024+ rows.

Sensitivity models vary the row rule, the working correlation, and the target convention. The era-standardized series is shown for completeness, but its level is not comparable with the fixed series.

```{r models}
read_extract <- function(path) {
  if (grepl("\\.(RData|rda)$", path, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
    e <- new.env(); load(path, envir = e); get(ls(e)[1], envir = e)
  } else {
    read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }
}
gee_prep <- function(dat, valcol) {
  x <- dat[!is.na(dat[[valcol]]) & !is.na(dat$age) & !is.na(dat$female) & !is.na(dat$nyha_hi), ]
  x$val <- x[[valcol]]
  x <- x[order(x$lopnr, x$year), ]
  x$yr <- x$year - 2014
  x$age_c <- x$age - 72
  x$nyha_hi <- as.integer(x$nyha_hi)
  x$pid <- as.integer(factor(x$lopnr))   # geepack is very slow with character cluster IDs
  x$h16 <- pmax(x$year - 2016, 0)
  x$h21 <- pmax(x$year - 2021, 0)
  x$h24 <- pmax(x$year - 2024, 0)
  x
}
gee_trend <- function(x, corstr, label) {
  fit <- geeglm(val ~ yr + age_c + female + nyha_hi, id = pid, data = x,
                family = gaussian(), corstr = corstr)
  b  <- coef(fit)["yr"]
  se <- sqrt(vcov(fit)["yr", "yr"])
  span <- max(x$year) - 2014   # years from 2014 to the last year in the data
  data.frame(model = label, working_corr = corstr,
             n_py = nrow(x), n_patients = length(unique(x$lopnr)),
             change_2014_to_latest = round(span * b, 2),
             lo_95 = round(span * (b - 1.96 * se), 2),
             hi_95 = round(span * (b + 1.96 * se), 2),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
pw_slopes <- function(x) {
  x$h16 <- pmax(x$year - 2016, 0)
  x$h21 <- pmax(x$year - 2021, 0)
  x$h24 <- pmax(x$year - 2024, 0)
  # The 2024 hinge is included only when the extract has 2024+ rows. Otherwise the
  # column is all zero and geeglm() fails (rank deficient; seen in the first run).
  has24 <- any(x$year >= 2024)
  terms <- c("yr", "h16", "h21", if (has24) "h24")
  fml <- as.formula(paste("val ~", paste(c(terms, "age_c", "female", "nyha_hi"), collapse = " + ")))
  fit <- geeglm(fml, id = pid, data = x, family = gaussian(), corstr = "exchangeable")
  b <- coef(fit)[terms]
  V <- vcov(fit)[terms, terms, drop = FALSE]
  # Era slopes as contrasts on the hinge terms (rows = eras; columns = yr, h16, h21, h24)
  L <- rbind(c(1, 0, 0, 0), c(1, 1, 0, 0), c(1, 1, 1, 0), c(1, 1, 1, 1))
  L <- L[, c("yr", "h16", "h21", "h24") %in% terms, drop = FALSE]
  n_era <- if (has24) 4 else 3
  est <- se <- rep(NA_real_, 4)
  for (i in seq_len(n_era)) {
    l <- L[i, ]
    est[i] <- sum(l * b)
    se[i]  <- sqrt(as.numeric(t(l) %*% V %*% l))
  }
  data.frame(era = c("2014-2015", "2016-2020", "2021-2023", "2024-2025"),
             slope_points_per_year = round(est, 2),
             lo_95 = round(est - 1.96 * se, 2),
             hi_95 = round(est + 1.96 * se, 2),
             note = ifelse(seq_len(4) <= n_era, "", "not estimable: no 2024 or later rows"),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

x_latest <- gee_prep(py3, "val")
raw_dat  <- read_extract(params$data_path)
P_alt    <- build_rows(raw_dat, !params$esc_all)
py3_alt  <- pick_py(P_alt$rows, "kcmo3", "latest")
alt_label <- if (params$esc_all) "S2: shfdb4 targets (alternate)" else "S2: ESC targets throughout"

trend_sens <- rbind(
  gee_trend(x_latest, "exchangeable", "Primary: fixed 3-class, latest row per year"),
  gee_trend(x_latest, "independence", "Independence working correlation"),
  gee_trend(gee_prep(py3_high, "val"), "exchangeable", "D10 sensitivity: highest row per year"),
  gee_trend(gee_prep(py3_first, "val"), "exchangeable", "S6: first row per year"),
  gee_trend(gee_prep(py3_alt, "val"), "exchangeable", alt_label),
  gee_trend(gee_prep(era_py, "era_val"), "exchangeable", "Era-standardized series (level not comparable)")
)
write_out(trend_sens, "gee_trend_sensitivity.csv", "n_py")
show_tab(suppress_small(trend_sens, "n_py"), "GEE trend estimates: change from 2014 to the last year (95% CI) in KCMO points (95% CI)")

pw <- pw_slopes(x_latest)
write_out(pw, "piecewise_slopes.csv")
show_tab(pw, "Piecewise linear slopes by guideline era (points per year, 95% CI)")
```

## 9. Table 5: non-core therapy (descriptive, outside the score)

Digoxin, sinus-node inhibitor (ivabradine), and any nitrate. Vericiguat and hydralazine/isosorbide dinitrate are not identifiable in the current dictionary (Q18).

```{r table5}
noncore <- py3 %>% group_by(year) %>% summarise(
  n_py = n(),
  pct_digoxin = round(100 * mean(dig), 1),
  pct_sinus_node_inhibitor_ivabradine = round(100 * mean(ivab), 1),
  pct_any_nitrate = round(100 * mean(nitr), 1),
  .groups = "drop")
write_out(noncore, "table5_noncore.csv", "n_py")
show_tab(suppress_small(noncore, "n_py"), "Table 5: non-core therapy, percent of patient-years (outside the score)")
```

## Limitations stated in this analysis

- Eligibility: all classes are treated as eligible (SAP L1). Contraindication fields are not available; this will be revisited once Q3 is answered.
- Prescribed, not taken: registry doses are prescribed doses.
- The fixed three-class series is the comparability check; the era-standardized series changes definition in 2021 (SGLT2i added), so its level is not comparable across that boundary.
- The registry does not record a reason for dose reduction, so down-titration is a dose change, not an intolerance.
- Population: outpatients with EF below 40 percent (D11) and HF duration of at least 90 days.
